 Judgment

This appeal is filed by the appellant/Insurance Company challenging the judgment and award dated 01.08.2014 passed in MVC.No.7678/2012 by the learned XII Additional Small Causes Judge and MACT, Bengaluru, challenging the quantum of compensation.

sentences.text: Brief facts of the case are that, on 02.06.2012 at about 5.15 p.m., the deceased- Prathap was proceeding in his motorcycle bearing No.KA-02-HH-7143 from East to West at Kanteerava Studio Main Road by following the traffic rules slowly and cautiously on the left side of the road, at that time, all of a sudden the driver of the offending lorry bearing No.KA-40-7780 has driven the same in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the motor cycle of the deceased, as a result, he was fell down and left side rear wheel of the lorry ran over the head of the deceased.

Due to the impact,
the deceased succumbed to the injuries.
Therefore, the claimants filed claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, before the Tribunal, seeking compensation.

3. Heard the arguments on both sides and perused the records.
4.
The Tribunal has awarded compensation under 'loss of dependency' taking the multiplier according to the NC: 2023:KHC:21422 age of the deceased.
It is the ground raised by the appellant/Insurance Company that the multiplier ought to have been taken according to the age of the claimant No.1- mother of the deceased.
Further, it has also raised a ground that the driver has not been made as party in the proceedings.
5. As per the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Smt.Sarla Verma & Others.

Vs.
Delhi Transport Corpn And Another reported in AIR 2009 SC 3104, the multiplier applicable in the case of death is to be assessed according to the age of the deceased, but not according to the age of the parents of the deceased.
Therefore, the Tribunal is correct in assessing the multiplier taking the age of the deceased.
Therefore, on this ground, the appeal is liable to be dismissed.
6. Insofar as not making the driver as a party in the proceedings, the driver is a proper party, but not NC: 2023:KHC:21422 necessary party.
The owner of the offending vehicle is made as party who is necessary party.
Therefore, as per Order I Rule 9 of CPC, the owner of the offending vehicle is made as party.
Therefore, even though the driver may be proper party, but not making the driver as party does not affect core of the case.
A 'necessary party' is one without whom, no order can be made effectively, whereas a 'proper party' is one in whose absence, an effective order can be made on the question involved in the proceeding.
Therefore, owner is necessary party who is made as party in the claim proceedings.

Therefore, just because driver is not made as party as he is the only proper party,
in the absence of whom, effective adjudication cannot be done, such contention cannot be accepted.
Therefore, non-making of proper party is not fatal to the claim proceedings.
Hence, on this ground also, appeal is liable to be dismissed.

7. Hence I pass the following;
